activity.notes: After Chinggis Khan's death in 1227, his second son Chagatai ruled the Central Asian appanage that became the basis of the later Chagatai Khanate. Contemporary and dynastic terminology is more complex than the mod's simple 'Chagatai Khan' label, so ATLAS records him as ruler of the Chagatai ulus and does not retroject a fully independent later khanate. Modern scholarship varies between 1241 and 1242 for his death, so the terminal year is approximate.

sources.title: Bruno De Nicola, The Queen of the Chaghatayids
sources.citation_text: The Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society notes that after Chinggis Khan died in 1227, Chaghatai became ruler of the Central Asian lands that formed the origin of the later Chaghataid Khanate.

review_context.correction_note: Use the contemporary appanage/ulus rather than anachronistically asserting a mature independent Chagatai Khanate.
